$meta.capturedWith: Playwright, getComputedStyle + getBoundingClientRect on the live site
$meta.theme: Themify 'Basic' WordPress theme, skin-default, body class 'sidebar1 default_width'
$meta.notes: All px values are the browser's computed values. Values like 14.4px, 19.2px, 22.4px, 28.8px come from em-based theme CSS on a 16px root, so in Tailwind they are best expressed as rem (0.9rem, 1.2rem, 1.4rem, 1.8rem) rather than rounded to the nearest whole pixel.

body.usedFor: body text, all headings, post titles, nav links, sidebar links, footer text, wordmark, tagline. This single value covers essentially every piece of text on the site.

onDark.usedFor: text inside the Subscribe button, the search Search button, pagination number chips, the back-to-top arrow, and the active nav item chip

mobileNavLink.usedFor: links inside the mobile hamburger dropdown only (<=1100px)

mobileNavLinkHover.usedFor: hover state of mobile dropdown links

hrDefault.usedFor: browser default hr colour, theme does not restyle hr
hrDefault.notes: No <hr> was found in real content; measured from an injected probe element.

usedFor: the 6px bar across the very top of every page (border-top on #headerwrap)
red.notes: This is the ONLY chromatic colour the theme applies. It is never used as a text colour or a link colour, only as the top bar and as an underline/hover tint. Defined in the WordPress Customizer custom CSS, not in the theme stylesheet.

header.usedFor: #headerwrap band behind the wordmark and nav

figcaption.usedFor: image caption strip under figures in post bodies

input.usedFor: search input and subscribe email input fills

button.usedFor: Subscribe button and search Search button

paginationChip.usedFor: pagination number chips (links only, the current page number has no fill)

activeNavChip.usedFor: the current menu item's pill in the main nav

hairline.usedFor: footer top rule, search input border, subscribe input border

sidebarRule.usedFor: bottom rule under the sidebar social-icons widget only (class .borderbottom, applied to one widget, not to widget headings)

imageFrame.usedFor: 1px border around in-content images (.wp-block-image img, img.size-full), paired with 4px padding to make a photo mat

table.usedFor: table cell top borders (1px) and th bottom border (2px)

color.notes: Links are NOT a different colour from body text. They are distinguished only by a light underline.

underlineDefault.notes: text-decoration-color, from custom CSS `a, a:link { text-decoration-color: #ccc; }`

underlineHover.notes: from custom CSS `a:hover { text-decoration-color: #cc4141; }`. The text colour does not change on hover, only the underline tint.

rssIcon.usedFor: the RSS glyph in the header social widget

sans.notes: Computed font-family is the bare string "Open Sans" with NO fallback stack. Faces are self-hosted/inlined by the Themify Google-Fonts optimiser as @font-face rules pointing at fonts.gstatic.com.

mono.notes: The theme sets no monospace family. <pre> and <code> fall back to the browser default monospace at 13px.

unusedLoaded.notes: Loaded by the font optimiser (400, 400i, 700) but not applied to anything measured. Probably a leftover Customizer selection. Safe to drop.

loadedWeights.notes: IMPORTANT: only 400 and 600 are actually loaded, but the CSS requests font-weight:700 for the wordmark, all headings, post titles and widget titles. The browser falls back to the 600 face. Rebuild with Open Sans 600 (or SemiBold) for anything the CSS calls 'bold', otherwise a real 700 face will look heavier than the live site.

html.notes: html rules are overridden by body; the Times value on html is inert

scale.notes: Body copy is 16px/24px. Everything else is an em multiple of that.
h1's line-height (32px = 1.0) is tighter than the h2-h6 pattern (1.3). Measured from injected probe elements inside .entry-content, because the sampled posts contain no real h1/h2/h3.

topAccentBar.notes: It is a border on the header wrapper, not a separate element, so it sits above the #F5F5F5 header band with no gap.

avatar.notes: Square, hard corners, black-and-white photo. The 100px left padding on hgroup is what clears the 85px image, giving a 15px gutter between the photo and the wordmark. Identical at all breakpoints - the avatar never shrinks.

wordmark.letterSpacingSource: -0.02em declared on #site-logo at 36px, inherited as px
wordmark.notes: The 40px line-height is much smaller than the 60px font-size, so the glyph box overflows its line box. This is why the wordmark visually overlaps the top of the header band. Reproduce the line-height literally or the header will grow taller than the original.

tagline.text: Microsoft Regional Director | Scrum Master | Speaker

socialWidget.content: a single RSS link (icon + the text 'RSS') pointing at https://adamcogan.com/feed/
socialWidget.mobileBehaviour: at <=1100px becomes position:static, float:none, padding:10px 0, so it drops onto its own full-width row above the nav

list.layout: floated <li>, horizontal, left aligned, full container width

link.notes: There is no left padding. The spacing between items is created entirely by 30px right padding plus 5px right margin, so the effective visual gap between one label's last letter and the next label's first letter is 35px. The <li> boxes touch: measured gap between adjacent <a> boxes is 5px.

hover.desktop: No hover rule exists for top-level nav links at desktop. Colour, background and decoration are unchanged on hover.

activeItem.customCssOverride: padding: 5px 10px; margin-right: 20px; (custom CSS wins over the theme's 5px 15px)
activeItem.notes: The home/blog listing page uses .current_page_parent, which is NOT matched by these selectors, so the homepage shows no highlighted nav item. On /about-adam-cogan/ the About item does get the dark pill. Reproduce that quirk or fix it deliberately.

mobile.hamburgerGlyph: 20x14 box built from a 2px black bottom-border plus ::before and ::after 2px bars

panel.display: none until #menu-icon is clicked (body gains class mobile_menu_active)

1440.columnPadding: 48.89px top / 29.33px bottom (5% and 3% of the 978px container)

768.notes: The sidebar has NOT stacked yet at 768. The stacking breakpoint is 760px.

390.columnPadding: 16.875px top / 10.125px bottom (5% and 3% of the 338px container)

breakpoints.1100: container switches from a fixed 978px to max-width:90%; #content 67.8% / #sidebar 26.2%; hamburger menu replaces the horizontal nav; .social-widget goes static
breakpoints.760: #content and #sidebar go float:none, width:100% !important, clear:both - the sidebar stacks below the main column
breakpoints.1200_and_1060: duplicate/overlapping rules for skin-page variants, not used by this site's skin-default body class
breakpoints.600: a screen and (max-width:600px) block exists in the theme CSS but does not change any layout measured here
breakpoints.notes: There is no breakpoint between 760 and 1100, so 768px-wide tablets get an awkward 178px sidebar. See OBSERVATIONS.md.

wrapper.notes: No divider rule between list items, only whitespace.

heroImage.notes: Fixed WordPress thumbnail size. Not every post has one - posts without a featured image simply start at the date line.

date.notes: Same size and colour as body copy. It is not dimmed or shrunk.

title.notes: 26px is a hard px value from the Customizer, not part of the em scale. The anchor inside is explicitly un-underlined by custom CSS.

meta.notes: The meta line is the same #333 as body text, only smaller. Category and tag links are comma-separated and wrap to multiple lines on posts with many tags, which is common.

postPage.structure: article.post > figure.post-image + div.post-content > time.post-date + h1.post-title + p.post-meta + div.entry-content

title.notes: The single-post h1 is 26px, the SAME size as a list item title, and SMALLER than a bare h1 in the body (32px). Archive and page titles (h1.page-title) are 32px. This inconsistency is in the original.

blockquote.notes: No left rule, no background, no quote mark. It is distinguished only by switching to italic Times. Measured from an injected probe - no blockquote appears in the sampled posts.

figure.notes: Custom CSS sets .wp-block-image { width: fit-content; display: grid; }

figureImage.notes: Applies to .wp-block-image img, .wp-caption img and img.size-full. Creates a subtle photo mat.

figcaption.notes: Bold text on a light grey strip flush under the image. Distinctive - do not lose this.

table.notes: Measured from an injected probe. No table appears in the sampled posts. Horizontal rules only, no vertical rules, no zebra striping, no header fill.

hr.notes: Theme does not style hr. Browser default 1px inset #808080, margin 8px 0.

wpBlockCode.whiteSpace: pre on the <pre>, pre-wrap on the inner <code>
wpBlockCode.notes: SURPRISE: code blocks are completely unstyled. No background fill, no padding, no border, no radius, no syntax highlighting. They read as slightly smaller monospace text sitting directly on the white page. Verified visually on /2025/08/12/net-aspire-cli-magic-and-developer-friendly-dashboards/. The markup is also malformed - a <code> nested inside another <code>.

inlineCode.notes: Also unstyled. Inline code is only distinguishable by the monospace face.

highlightingCodeBlockPlugin.status: installed and its stylesheet loads on every page, but no sampled post uses it
highlightingCodeBlockPlugin.preStyles: line-height 1.5, letter-spacing .1px, tab-size 4, overflow auto, padding var(--hcb--pY) var(--hcb--pX), border-radius 3px, background #f8f6f6
highlightingCodeBlockPlugin.notes: Worth auditing the full post corpus for .hcb_wrap before deciding whether to port these styles. If some older posts use it, the rebuild needs two code-block treatments.

postNav.layout: previous post on the left, next post on the right

floatingShareButtons.notes: A fixed vertical strip of Facebook / Twitter / LinkedIn squares pinned to the left edge of the viewport on single posts and pages. At desktop it sits in the empty left margin. At 390px it overlaps the article text. See OBSERVATIONS.md - probably should not be ported as-is.

title.textContent: the bare term name, e.g. 'General' - no 'Category:' prefix

archivePage.listing: identical markup and styling to the homepage listing

chipCurrent.notes: The CURRENT page is the plain one and the other pages are the filled black chips. That is inverted from the usual convention - verify before copying.

pagination.controls: numbered pages, then a next chevron, then a last-page chevron

aboutPage.sidebar: present, identical to every other page
aboutPage.content: a single .entry-content of paragraphs, no headings at all - it uses bold lead-in words (Clients, Scrum, ...) instead of headings

widget.notes: The only widget with a rule is the social-icons one, which carries an extra .borderbottom class giving it border-bottom: 1px solid #DDDDDD. Widget headings themselves have no underline or rule.

heading.notes: Headings are NOT uppercased and have no divider under them. Two different heading levels are used for the same visual role - h4.widgettitle for classic widgets and h5.wp-block-heading for block widgets - but both compute to 19.2px/700 so they look identical.

link.fontWeight: 400 (forced by custom CSS `#sidebar a { font-weight: normal }`)

subscribeWidget.title: Subscribe via email
subscribeWidget.body: Enter your email address to subscribe to this blog and receive notifications of new posts by email.
subscribeWidget.notes: The Subscribe button is a full pill (9999px) but the Search button right below it is a 5px rounded rectangle, despite identical fill, text colour and padding. Both come from WordPress core block defaults rather than the theme. Decide whether to unify them in the rebuild.

backToTop.content: an up-arrow glyph, text-indent -900em to hide the label
backToTop.notes: It sits inside the footer above the credit line, not fixed to the viewport.

right.html: Powered by WordPress | Built by SSW
right.plain: Powered by WordPress | Built by SSW

text.verbatim:
© Adam Cogan 2026
Powered by WordPress | Built by SSW
text.notes: The year 2026 is dynamic. At 390px the two blocks stack, left block first.

customCssWorthPorting.caption: .wp-caption-text, .wp-block-image figcaption { font-weight: bold; padding: .25rem .5rem; background: #f5f5f5; color: inherit; margin-top: 0 }
customCssWorthPorting.imageMat: .wp-block-image img, .wp-caption img, img.size-full { border: 1px solid #f5f5f5; padding: .25rem; box-sizing: border-box }
customCssWorthPorting.activeNav: #main-nav .current_page_item a, #main-nav .current-menu-item a { background: #333; color: #fff; padding: 5px 10px; margin-right: 20px }
customCssWorthPorting.progressTracker: ol.progtrckr - a step tracker with yellowgreen done / silver todo states, used on at least one post
customCssWorthPorting.notes: There is also an error-message style using an uploaded error.png sprite. Audit the post corpus before deciding whether .greybox and ol.progtrckr are worth porting.
